questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The size of the city - not too small, not too big. And the fact that I'd never been in Turin before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't that easy. I had to write my professors on certain occasions. The italian university system is a lot different than the danish system. That being said, there wasn't a need for a lot of information. You just had to show up in class and listen carefully, and most things would be explained.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a "contact person" who helped me and the other Erasmus students. And I could always ask at the Infopoint, if I had any doubts.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was tough. I was lucky. My advice is that you shouldn't get high hopes for an apartment of your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You don't necessarily get a contract

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Well I guess everything went smoothly. I chose my courses when I was still studying in Denmark. I had to change one course in my learning agreement, but that was fairly easy. Upon arrival I headed to the Infopoint and they registered my arrival. After that I was enrolled in my courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Infopoint, my Erasmus "buddy" and I could also contact the coordinator from UNITO if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, it seemed quite easy, but you don't get a lot of info if you don't ask for it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses varied. If was difficult to know what to expect at the exam. I didn't know what to read either. Everyone else in class were writing almost everything the teacher said down.  In some philosophy classes so many philosophers were introduced to us students, that remebering all of them seemed a bit unrealistic. Quality-wise, the level of teaching was rather low on most courses. The students just had to take notes and remember them by heart. But in the end the exams were quite easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We didn't work in groups, which I was getting used to in Copenhagen. We had to take a lot of notes, which I never felt was necessary before. At UNITO, the students rarely ask questions to the teacher. The communication is rather one-way, whereas at UCPH we have conversations with the teacher and our classmates. I prefer the classes at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
STU0490 Language, text and speech (6)
FIL0310 Aesthetics (6)
FIL0002 History of Russian Philosophy (6)
STS0176 Contemporary history and history of journalism (12)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contemporary history and history of journalism - very good professors.

questions.answer: Food is more expensive than expected in Italy, especially if you like good quality cheese.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think there were some sport acitivities available, but I never went. Flyers were handed out in front of the university with theater workshops and things like that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I got some fine experiences from rowing on the river Po.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed going out of the city, especially to the mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I study italian culture in Denmark, so I wasn't that difficult to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really, they are quite young the students in Turin, much younger than me.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes italians can be quite narrow-sighted.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the oldschool Italy, the nice trattorie and osterie. Dining at an old cozy restaurant is something special.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) find someone to practice your italian with
2) go for daytrips out of the city to see the beautiful countryside
3) use the markets

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The trips to the mountains

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
